title: Orsen and the Veil
premise: When the crown of Veyland declares the Purging of Gifts, Rosalind Halloran flees her master's burning cottage and discovers the smugglers' roads she knows so well are the last threads of a spell: the Veil, a concealment woven by the old kingdom of Thornfell before it was erased from maps and memory. Guided by Orsen, a disgraced royal cartographer who once helped draw the country out of existence, she must gather the scattered keystones of the Veil before the last dragon, whose fire sustains it, dies. Betrayed by the friend who sold her name to the crown's witch-hunters, Rosalind must choose between restoring Thornfell at the cost of every life in Veyland or letting a nation stay dead to save the living. In the end she rewrites the Veil not as a wall but as a door, making Thornfell a country that exists only for those who choose to cross.
about_author: Paloma Almeida is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six years leading treks through mountain passes that appear on no modern map. She writes fantasy about borders, both the kind drawn on paper and the kind drawn through the heart.

chapters.title: Ash on the Windward Road
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She returns from a smuggling run to find her master's cottage burned and a crown proclamation nailed to the gate: all gifted persons to be surrendered. She escapes with her master's grimoire and a strange brass key he pressed into her hand. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A disgraced court cartographer drinking himself blind in a border town recognizes the key Rosalind carries when she tries to sell it. He tells her it opens something that officially does not exist. Emotional beat: shame meeting a chance at redemption.

chapters.title: Witch-Hunters at the Ford
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Crown hunters nearly catch them at a river crossing; Rosalind uses a hedge-charm to flood the ford, revealing her gift publicly for the first time. Orsen sees what she can do. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into defiant self-knowledge.

chapters.title: What the Maps Forgot
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In an abandoned survey station, Orsen confesses his role in the Unmapping: he drew the borders that erased Thornfell after its king refused to kneel. The Veil was the kingdom's dying curse and shield. Emotional beat: confession as the first step toward trust.

chapters.title: The Smuggler Who Sold Her Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her oldest friend and fellow smuggler, Dain, appears offering safe passage — but Rosalind realizes he is the informant who betrayed her master. She says nothing and lets him travel with them. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into watchful suspicion.

chapters.title: Keystone in the Deepwood
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They recover the first keystone from a shrine swallowed by forest, waking a guardian wight that tests Rosalind's intent rather than her strength. The keystone shows her a vision of living Thornfell. Emotional beat: longing for a home she never had.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. High in the mountains they witness the sky flicker where the Veil thins — the last dragon's fire is failing, and whole valleys briefly blink between existence and erasure. Emotional beat: dread at a deadline made visible.

chapters.title: Dain's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Cornered by witch-hunters, Dain trades information again: their route and Rosalind's destination, in exchange for his own pardon. He tells himself it is mercy, not betrayal. Emotional beat: self-deception dressed as love.

chapters.title: The Salt Cathedral
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Beneath a salt mine lies the second keystone, guarded by descendants of Thornfell's exiles who have kept the faith for a generation. Their elder offers Rosalind the truth: restoring the kingdom requires a life freely given to the dragon's fire. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Ambush at Graywater Pass
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Witch-hunters strike using Dain's intelligence; Orsen is captured, and Rosalind barely escapes with both keystones. She learns the hunters' captain is gifted herself, serving the crown to survive. Emotional beat: rage and the temptation to become what hunts her.

chapters.title: The Captain's Mirror
chapters.summary: Captain Ilse Vane's POV. Interrogating Orsen, Ilse reveals she hides her own gift behind the hunt's banner; she offers Orsen a deal — help her reach the dragon first, and she will bury the truth of what the crown intends for the Veil. Emotional beat: complicity recognizing itself.

chapters.title: Alone with the Grimoire
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Hiding in a shepherd's hut, Rosalind deciphers her master's marginalia and learns he was born in Thornfell, one of the Unmapped, and raised her deliberately as the Veil's possible heir. Emotional beat: orphanhood transformed into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Confession
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Dain, sick with guilt, finds Rosalind and confesses everything, then offers to lead the hunters astray — a plan that will likely cost him his life. Rosalind cannot forgive him but accepts the sacrifice. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth resolved into costly honesty.

chapters.title: Fire Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Following the dragon's fading heat, they enter the caldera of Old Thornfell's capital, which exists only inside the Veil: streets, bones, and banners intact under ash. Emotional beat: awe and horror walking hand in hand.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In the palace ruins they find Serevanth, the last dragon, ancient and nearly flameless, sustained only by the two keystones Rosalind carries. He explains the choice: feed him a willing life and Thornfell lives; let him die and the Veil falls forever. Emotional beat: the weight of a decision no one should carry alone.

chapters.title: Ilse at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Captain Vane arrives with her hunters and Orsen as prisoner, intending to seize the keystones for the crown — but seeing the dead city, her conviction cracks. She turns her blade on her own lieutenant instead. Emotional beat: a hunter choosing a side at last.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Freed, Orsen argues the kingdom's restoration would doom Veyland's borderlands to war and famine; Rosalind accuses him of wanting absolution more than truth. They part angry on the eve of the ritual. Emotional beat: trust broken precisely when unity matters most.

chapters.title: Serevanth's Hunger
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The dragon weakens past the point of choice; without fire soon, the Veil collapses violently, killing everyone within miles. Rosalind prepares to give her own life, writing a letter she may never send. Emotional beat: quiet, terrified resolve.

chapters.title: The Door, Not the Wall
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. At the moment of sacrifice, Rosalind refuses the binary: using her master's key and her hedge-craft, she reweaves the Veil mid-ritual into a threshold rather than a fortress, drawing power from every exile's willing memory instead of one death. Serevanth's fire roars back; the city breathes. Emotional beat: defiance of fate through imagination.

chapters.title: What Rises from Ash
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Thornfell re-emerges as a small, open country — visible on new maps Orsen draws himself, open to any who choose to cross. Ilse defects with half her hunters; Dain, wounded but alive, carries the news south. Emotional beat: hard-won, imperfect hope.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Mark
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Standing at the new border-gate, Rosalind buries her master's letter beside the road and takes up his grimoire as teacher to the exiles' gifted children. She forgives Orsen, not fully, but enough. Emotional beat: grief integrated into purpose.

chapters.title: A Country That Chooses You Back
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Rosalind's POV. Years later, travelers line the mountain roads seeking the door in the Veil; some are turned away, most are welcomed. Rosalind watches from the gatehouse, the last dragon's fire steady on the horizon. Emotional beat: belonging earned, never given.
